prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, hip-cut demi statue portrait, a four-wedge fan-sliced multi-material body, every material seam physically stepped. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh-stub tips just below her hip line, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Korean woman in girl-crush makeup — fair ivory skin, sharply angled thin brows, a razor-sharp winged cat-eye liner extending far past the outer corner, deep brown-black eyeshadow, long lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, strongly sculpted contour, a deep wine-red matte lip, long sleek black hair, a cold, commanding gaze. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a big black-steel hoop and a thick bar.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, a waistline that still pulls in sharply, then an enormous belly and colossal wide hips flaring out again, her body a four-wedge fan of crystal, stone, glass-vessel and wood, each wedge physically stepped from the next.

Boundary (skin to material, at the collarbones): a single straight, flat line runs around the base of her neck and across both collarbones, nowhere lower, never reaching her chest — never jagged, never zigzag, a clean straight cut like a cross-section. Real skin above this straight line, the material immediately below it. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow.

Her whole body below the collarbones is divided into four wedge-shaped slices, like a sliced pie, all meeting at a single point at the centre of her chest and fanning outward and downward to her shoulders, hips and both thigh-stubs. Slice one (toward her left shoulder and arm): solid transparent crystal, solid golden-yellow citrine crystal, with faint feathery inclusions and colour zoning, deep honey-gold where thickest and pale lemon at every thin edge. Slice two (toward her right shoulder and arm): carved from genuine turquoise, a vivid sky-blue to blue-green stone laced with fine dark matrix veining, polished to a smooth, cool sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque. Slice three (toward her left hip and thigh-stub): a sculpted vessel of clear glass (unmistakably glass, crystal-clear and polished, bright specular reflections) filled with clear rose-pink water holding a scattered handful of deep red rose petals drifting slowly, sealing shut at its thigh-stub tip. Slice four (toward her right hip and thigh-stub): carved from dark wenge wood, a deep near-black wood finely striped with narrow gold-tan pinstripes, polished to a hard satin sheen, completely opaque, completely opaque, rounding off at its thigh-stub tip. At every seam where two different materials meet, one material's edge rises very slightly above its neighbour, catching a thin, crisp shadow line — this tiny physical step, repeated at every single boundary in this pattern, is what proves each piece is a truly separate object, not a flat pattern painted onto one continuous surface.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft cream white on one side and a deep crimson red on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand (crystal) resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so white light glances off one side and red light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint of shadow along every stepped seam, light passing straight through the crystal and vessel wedges while only reflecting off the stone and wood wedges. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
